walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Composing — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Composing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Composing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
It is always C major.
Entirely new material is introduced.

mcqs.q: What happens in the recapitulation of sonata form?
options: Entirely new material is introduced.
It is always C major.
Both subjects return, but the second subject is now in the tonic key.
The exposition is repeated exactly.

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
Any two phrases of similar style.
A long melody with no breaks.
Entirely new material is introduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crotchet (quarter note)”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dotted note”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semibreve (whole note)”?
options: Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Note value”?
options: Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quaver (eighth note)”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rest”?
options: Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.

mcqs.q: How many quavers equal a crotchet?
options: 4 quavers
2 quavers
5 quavers
3 quavers
